articles.title: TikTok watermarked vs clean: what the API options really mean
articles.excerpt: When I wired TikTok downloads into ramrom.io, I assumed there would be one video file per link. Paste the link, get the MP4, done. The provider's API had other ideas. It offered two versions of the sa…
articles.body: When I wired TikTok downloads into ramrom.io, I assumed there would be one video file per link. Paste the link, get the MP4, done. The provider's API had other ideas. It offered two versions of the same video: one with a watermark, one without. Choosing between them turned out to be one of the more interesting decisions in the whole downloader, because the two files are not made the same way at all. What the watermark actually is A TikTok watermark is not a picture stamped over the video after the fact. It is baked into the video file TikTok serves to the web player. When you watch a TikTok in a browser, the file you are watching already has the username and the logo bouncing around the frame.

articles.title: Two AI Agents Reviewed the Same PR. Was That Actually Independent?
articles.excerpt: Imagine this workflow: Agent A writes a patch and opens a pull request. Agent B reviews it and says "LGTM." CI turns green. Two agents, one approved PR. Sounds like independent review. Now change a fe…
articles.body: Imagine this workflow: Agent A writes a patch and opens a pull request. Agent B reviews it and says "LGTM." CI turns green. Two agents, one approved PR. Sounds like independent review. Now change a few details. Both agents can modify the same workspace. The reviewer relies on the author's generated summary. The tested commit might not be the commit that ultimately gets merged. Do we still have independent verification, or just two agreeing opinions? I'm increasingly interested in the boundaries that make a review independent, rather than simply the number of models involved. For example, a reviewer could use a read-only checkout pinned to an exact commit, inspect the raw diff, and verify which tests actually executed. That gives us evidence the implementing agent cannot simply rewrite.

articles.body: MetaのQuest 2時代が終わる——それは「VR科学」の終わりではなく、次の章の始まり MetaがQuest 2とQuest Proのサポート終了を発表しました。両機種は来年初頭に最後のOSアップデートを受け取り、来春に控えるMeta VR Glassesへ向けて、同社はHorizonOSの開発リソースを新しいハードウェアへ移していく方針を示しています。 このニュースを見て「VRはもう下火なのか」と受け取った人もいるかもしれません。しかし、教育や研究の現場でVRを使ってきた立場から見ると、これはむしろ逆の合図です。ハードウェアの世代交代は、その上で動くソフトウェアが“汎用のデモ”から“専門的なワークフローの一部”へ進化するタイミングだからです。プラットフォームが変わるたびに、生き残るのは「そのデバイスでしか成立しない体験」です。そして分子科学ほど、その条件に近い領域はありません。 フラットな画面に閉じ込められてきた構造生物学 構造生物学の日々の仕事を思い浮かべてください。タンパク質の立体構造は、いまも多くの場合、フラットなモニタ上でマウスによって回転させられ、論文用の図として切り取られます。しかし、結合ポケットの奥行き、リガンドの向き、電子密度の重なり、水素結合の角度——これらの情報は本来、紙の上や画面の中でなく、その構造の“中に立って”見るべきものです。 エンジニアの言葉で言えば、これは「次元の圧縮」です。3次元のデータを2次元の射影に落とすとき、奥行きの情報は失われます。回転させて角度を変えれば補える——そう考えるかもしれませんが、視点操作のたびに頭の中で座標変換を走らせるのは、人間の認知にとって安い処理ではありません。特に結合ポケットの内部のように、複数の残基が狭い空間で絡み合う領域では、この変換コストが理解のボトルネックになります。 教育の場面でも同じです。ヘモ…

articles.title: I built AiRap.me: turn one photo into a lip-synced AI rap video
articles.excerpt: Earlier this year my feed was full of AI rap videos: someone's selfie, their cat, or a cartoon character dropping a verse. When I tried to make one myself, it took a whole toolchain: one tool for lyri…
articles.body: Earlier this year my feed was full of AI rap videos: someone's selfie, their cat, or a cartoon character dropping a verse. When I tried to make one myself, it took a whole toolchain: one tool for lyrics, another for the song, a lip-sync app, then a video editor to put it all together. Most "AI rap generators" also stop at an audio file, but what people actually share is a video . So I built AiRap.me : upload one photo, pick a style, and get a finished rap video back, usually in about 20–30 seconds. What it does One photo in, rap video out. The AI writes an original verse, makes the beat, generates the vocals and lip-syncs the face in your photo. You don't need a song, a voice recording or an editing app. Solo or duo. Use one photo, or two photos where two performers trade verses.

articles.body: If you haven’t watched the Street Fighter League Americas 2026 Finals , you’re missing out. It is — and I say this with complete sincerity — some of the best competitive Street Fighter I have ever seen in my life, mostly owing to a heart-stopping set between Derek ‘Blaz’ and Noah ‘NoahTheProdigy’ Solis. Blaz, a 17-year-old Chilean phenom, broke into the scene with a bang when he was just 14 years old. At 15, he got second place at Capcom Cup — the world’s most competitive Street Fighter tournament — and at 16, he secured third place. During this time, Latin America as a region became extremely strong in Street Fighter 6 , with figures like 15-year-old Chilean player Craime making Top 8 at Evo Las Vegas this year and winning the 2026 Esports World Cup for the game.
articles.author: Virginia Glaze
